recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only if the module diagram is redesigned or the work group explicitly chooses to remove the three-group summary despite the later level-label decision.
issue_request: FHIR-31576 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for the FHIR-core Getting Started modules page. It reported that the text describing Infrastructure as the bottom rung/bottom row, Content as the middle rung/top row, and Reasoning as the top rung contradicted the diagram, and the recorded resolution said to remove that confusing three-group text.
initial_application: No source commit explicitly tagged FHIR-31576 was found. The old wording remained until commit dfb07285cbc2261914990d8de6a9ac750a96d594, titled for FHIR-33977, rewrote the three bullets in source/modules.html to Infrastructure (Level 1 and Level 2), Content (Level 3 and Level 4), and Reasoning (Level 5).
additional_context: FHIR-33977 later reached Published/Persuasive with Modification and explicitly approved the current level-label wording for the same Modules page mismatch. FHIR-31612 raised the same diagram/text direction problem and is already audited on the combined branch as satisfied by the FHIR-33977 application. source/hierarchy.xml lists modules.html as Getting Started, and source/modules.html includes source/modules-fragment.html, whose diagram labels Levels 1 through 5. Confluence refs found FHIR-I meeting minutes for the FHIR-31576 and FHIR-33977 votes, and bounded Zulip searches found no conflicting discussion.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Removing the current level-label bullets would contradict the later accepted FHIR-33977 resolution without improving implementer understanding; the current source no longer contains the misleading rung/row descriptors that triggered FHIR-31576.
